short_description: The rain ahead for your spot as a timeline: turn the wheel to look from the next hour to the next two days.
description:
# Buitje

The rain ahead for your spot, at a glance.

On the front display rain hangs down from a time axis: a sparse sprinkle for drizzle, a dense block for a downpour. Now is at the left. Turn the wheel to choose how far ahead it looks, from the next hour to the next two days.

The back display says what is coming in a sentence, such as "Drizzle for about 45 minutes" or "Dry until 22:35", and shows all 48 hours as a strip with a frame around what the front shows.

## Controls

- **Wheel:** sets the window: 1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36 or 48 hours. Left alone for half a minute it goes back to your default.
- **OK:** switches between the timeline and the headline in two lines, such as RAIN IN / 15 MIN.
- **Start:** asks for fresh data.
- **Back:** leaves the app.

The status light blinks blue when rain is about to start.

## Where it works

Anywhere, but it is made for the Netherlands and Belgium, and best there.

- **The Netherlands and Belgium:** the next 2 hours from the rain radar, in steps of 5 minutes, then a 2 km weather model for the 2 days after.
- **The rest of central and northern Europe:** no radar; a 5.5 km weather model, by the quarter for the first 3 hours.
- **The rest of the world:** no radar; a weather model by the hour.

The app finds out by itself which of these it is in.

## Settings

- **Place:** the spot the rain is shown for; Utrecht until you set it. After detecting it automatically, check that it names your town: rain is local.
- **Window:** how far ahead the timeline looks when the app starts.
- **Rain alert:** how long before rain the status light blinks: off, or 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes. A sound can go with it.
- **Language:** English or Nederlands.

The app reads its settings when it starts, so start it again after a change.

## Good to know

- The bar needs Wi-Fi. Without it the app says so and waits. When the connection drops it keeps showing what it had, marked as old and with the time it is from, for up to 3 hours.
- It only says what it knows: when part of the forecast is missing, the timeline's axis ends where the data does.
- Rain data: [Buienradar](https://www.buienradar.nl) for the radar, and [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com) with KNMI's HARMONIE model for the forecast.
- Tested on a BUSY Bar with firmware 1.4.1 and on BUSY Bar Emulator with firmware 1.3.1.
changelog: First release: the rain timeline with a window of 1 to 48 hours on the wheel, the headline in words, a 48-hour strip on the back display, an alert before rain starts, English and Dutch, and plain messages when the connection is gone.
